en.content: This herb only grows on the shadowed face of the cliff — a handful of stalks a year. The town physicians can write the prescription, but not one of them will climb down for it. My life's dangled on a rope over that drop for twenty years — not so anyone remembers me, but for the stranger in the valley waiting on this dose to keep breathing. He doesn't know my name. That's fine.
en.editorNote: For a cliff-climbing herb-gatherer period still, or for the person doing the unseen, dangerous work that quietly keeps someone else alive.
variations: Anyone can copy the prescription. Lowering yourself over the cliff to actually pick it — all these years, that's still just me.

items.sourceNote: 古裝虐戀放河燈「為活人留燈、意難平」BE 思念母題 register 參考，內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 每年這一夜，我做的燈最多，也放得最遠。人人都以為河燈是替死去的人引路，只有我知道——我放的那盞，是想替一個還活著、卻再也不會回頭的人，照亮回家的路。他要真肯回來，一盞就夠；他若不回，我做一整條河也是白費。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配放河燈、中元或元宵的古裝劇照，或寫給那個「你早就走遠、我還在原地替你留燈」的意難平。
variations: 這滿河的燈，別人數的是願望，我數的是你沒回來的年頭。

en.content: On this one night each year, I make the most lanterns and float mine the farthest. Everyone thinks river lanterns light the way for the dead. Only I know mine is trying to light the road home for someone still alive who will never turn back. If he ever meant to come, one lantern is enough. If he doesn't, I could float a whole river and it would all be for nothing.
en.editorNote: For a floating-lantern festival period still, or for the ache of keeping a light burning for someone long gone who won't look back.
variations: This whole river of lanterns — others count wishes on them; I count the years you haven't come home.

items.sourceNote: 古裝宮廷畫師「憑思念作畫、藏而不裱」深情曖昧母題 register 參考，內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 陛下命我畫盡宮中美人，一幅一幅，我從沒畫錯過一張臉。可只有一個人，我閉著眼也能畫——不必看她坐在哪，不必等她抬頭，那眉眼早就一筆一筆，長在我心裡了。這樣的畫，我只敢藏，不敢裱。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配宮廷畫師、丹青的古裝劇照，或送給那個「你的樣子我早就背得滾瓜爛熟」的曖昧對象。
variations: 滿宮的人我照著畫，只有你，我是憑著想念畫的。

en.content: His Majesty had me paint every beauty in the palace — one portrait after another, and I've never once gotten a face wrong. But there's one person I could paint with my eyes shut. I don't need her to sit for me, don't need her to look up; those brows, those eyes were painted into my heart long ago, stroke by stroke. A painting like that I only dare to hide — never to mount and hang.
en.editorNote: For a court-painter or ink-brush period still, or for the crush whose face you already know by heart.
variations: Everyone else in the palace I paint from life. Only you I paint from missing you.

items.sourceNote: 反套路穿書/雙穿越喜劇（現代靈魂穿古、聯手逆天改命）register 參考，內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 書上寫我是禍國妖妃，第三章就該領盒飯。可作者大概沒算到——我看過結局，也認得你這個同樣穿進來的倒楣蛋。既然劇本爛成這樣，那咱們就別照著演了，改天翻它個底朝天。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配穿書、反套路喜劇的古裝劇照，或送給那個「跟你一起把爛牌打成好牌」的隊友。
variations: 劇本說我活不過三章，我偏要拉著你演到大結局。
都穿進同一本爛書了，不如我們合夥把它改寫成喜劇。

en.content: The book says I'm the wicked consort who dooms the kingdom — written off by chapter three. But the author never counted on this: I've read the ending, and I recognize you, the other poor soul who fell in here. If the script's this bad, let's stop following it and flip the whole thing on its head.
en.editorNote: For a transmigration-comedy or reverse-trope period still, or for the teammate you turn a bad hand into a winning one with.
variations: The script says I don't survive past chapter three — so I'll drag you all the way to the finale instead.
We both fell into the same terrible book; might as well team up and rewrite it as a comedy.

items.sourceNote: 仙俠甜虐「剋夫命格/契約婚」母題 register 參考，內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 都說我命裡剋夫，靠近的人不是走就是傷。你偏偏立在我面前，說要跟我簽三年契約。我勸你別——你卻笑著把手遞過來：「那正好，我這條命本來就不長，剋壞了也不虧，剋不壞，就當賺了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配仙俠契約婚、命格虐戀的古裝劇照，或形容「明知會受傷還是選你」的那種偏執。
variations: 世人怕我的命，你偏把命交到我手裡。
我說我剋夫，你說那我們比比看，是你的命硬，還是我的狠。

en.content: They all say I'm cursed to ruin any husband — whoever gets close either leaves or gets hurt. You stood in front of me anyway, offering a three-year contract. I told you not to. You just smiled and held out your hand: "Perfect. My life was never going to be long — if the curse takes it, no loss; if it doesn't, call it a windfall."
en.editorNote: For a xianxia contract-marriage or fated-tragedy still, or for that stubborn "I chose you knowing it would hurt" feeling.
variations: The whole world fears my fate — and you put your life in my hands anyway.
I said I'd ruin any man I marry; you said let's find out whose fate is tougher, yours or mine.

items.sourceNote: 大女主經商/家業題材（女子撐起商號、以算盤為劍）register 參考，內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 他們笑我一個女子也想撐起這間商號，說賬房裡沒有女人的位子。我只回一句：這鋪子裡每一筆進出，每一條銀路，都是我一手算出來的。你們搶得走招牌，搶不走我腦子裡這本賬——沒有我，這門檻，你們連跨都跨不進。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配大女主經商、女掌櫃的古裝劇照，或送給那個「靠本事把場子撐起來」的職場女性。
variations: 算盤是我的劍，賬本是我的兵，這江山我用銀子也照樣打下來。
你們讓我退到後宅，我偏要把整條街的生意握在手心。

en.content: They laughed that a woman thinks she can carry this whole trading house — said the counting room has no seat for a woman. I gave them one answer: every coin in and out of this shop, every silver route, I worked out with my own hand. You can seize the signboard, but you can't seize the ledger in my head — without me, you can't even step over the threshold.
en.editorNote: For a female-lead merchant or lady-proprietor period still, or for the woman who built her standing on sheer skill.
variations: The abacus is my sword and the ledger is my army — I can win this empire in silver too.
You told me to retreat to the inner court; instead I'll hold the whole street's trade in my palm.

items.sourceNote: 亂世權謀/絕境奔命（限期護送、廟堂之外的孤勇）register 參考，內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 廟堂上的人只看得見一座城的得失，我卻要在十五日內，帶著這滿城人的性命，從南跑到北。沒有人替我撐傘，沒有人替我留門。可只要我還有一口氣，這條路，我就替他們走到底。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配亂世權謀、奔命護送的古裝劇照，或送給那個「扛著一群人往前走、卻沒人替他撐傘」的人。
variations: 朝堂在算一座城，我在算一條命也不能少。
沒人替我留門，我就自己把這條路走成一條門。

en.content: The men at court can only see the gain or loss of a single city; I have fifteen days to carry a whole city's lives from the south to the north. No one holds an umbrella over me, no one leaves a door open for me. But as long as I still have breath, I'll walk this road to the end for them.
en.editorNote: For a wartime-intrigue or desperate-escort period still, or for the one carrying a crowd forward with no one shielding them.
variations: The court is counting one city; I'm counting so that not one life is lost.
No one leaves a door open for me — so I'll walk this road until it becomes one.

items.sourceNote: 邊關戍守/家書抵萬金 register 參考（塞北從軍、寫給家中人的未寄之信母題），內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 塞北的風把我寫給你的信吹散了一頁又一頁。他們說家書抵萬金，可我這封信不敢寫太滿——怕寫得太想你，就沒力氣再守下去了。等仗打完，我把這些沒寄出去的字，一句一句，念到你耳邊。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配邊關從軍、久別重逢的古裝劇照，或寫給那個「在遠方咬牙撐著、報喜不報憂」的人。
variations: 我把想你兩個字，壓在盔甲最裡層，怕它一露出來，我就想回家了。
烽火連天我都不怕，就怕這封信寄到時，你已經等成了另一個模樣。

en.content: The northern wind tears my letters to you away, page after page. They say a letter from home is worth a fortune in war — but I don't dare fill mine, afraid that if I write how much I miss you, I'll lose the strength to hold this line. When the war is over, I'll read every unsent word to you, one by one, against your ear.
en.editorNote: For a frontier-soldier or long-separation period still, or for the one gritting it out far away who only ever sends the good news.
variations: I've buried the words 'I miss you' in the deepest layer of my armor — afraid that the moment they show, I'll turn for home.
I don't fear a sky full of war-fires; I fear that by the time this letter reaches you, you've waited yourself into someone I no longer know.

items.sourceNote: 求而不得/白月光 register 參考（心口那顆得不到的硃砂痣母題），內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 你是我這一生都沒能娶進門的那個人。旁人以為我什麼都有了——高官、厚祿、滿府的燈。只有我自己知道，那盞一直沒點亮的，才是我真正想守的一盞。你是我心口最白的那道月光，遠遠照著，卻從來不落在我身上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配求而不得、意難平的古裝劇照，或形容那個「這輩子最好、卻永遠差一步」的人。
variations: 別人問我為何後院常空著一間房，我說那是替一個沒來的人，留的。
我把整座府邸都點亮了，唯獨留一盞燈，等一個不會回頭的你。

en.content: You're the one I never managed to bring home in this whole life. Others think I have everything — rank, fortune, a manor full of lanterns. Only I know the one lamp I never lit is the one I truly wanted to keep. You're the palest moonlight over my heart — shining from far away, never once falling on me.
en.editorNote: For an unrequited or "the one that got away" period still, or for the person who was the best thing in your life and always one step out of reach.
variations: When they ask why one room in my courtyard stays empty, I say it's kept for someone who never came.
I lit up the whole manor and left a single lamp burning — waiting for a you who will never look back.

items.sourceNote: 2026 武俠雙強互撕甜虐（《江湖夜雨十年燈》雙面少主×佛系女俠、撕假面）register 參考，內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 整個江湖都在戴假面，就你一個人，敢當著我的面把我的面具摘下來。我防了所有人，唯獨在你這裡，防到一半就懶了——反正你早就看穿，我這身狠，是裝給別人看的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配武俠雙強、歡喜冤家CP的古裝劇照，或形容那個「別人面前刀槍不入、在他面前繳械投降」的關係。
variations: 我對全天下都留三分戒心，對你只留半分，剩下那兩分半，是想留給你，不是留著防你。
你最討厭我裝，可你不知道，我唯一沒裝的那一面，一直是為你留的。

en.content: The whole jianghu wears a mask — you're the only one who dares pull mine off to my face. I keep my guard up against everyone, but with you I give up halfway; you saw through it long ago anyway — all this ruthlessness of mine is a costume I put on for other people.
en.editorNote: For a dual-lead wuxia or bickering-rivals CP still, or for the relationship where you're untouchable to the world and disarmed the second they walk in.
variations: I keep three parts of my guard up against all the world and only half a part against you — and the rest I'm saving to give you, not to defend against you.
You hate that I put on an act — but you don't know the one face I never faked has always been kept for you.

items.sourceNote: 帝王/權謀情話「山河為聘」register 參考（以整個天下作聘禮母題），內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 別人娶你，抬十里紅妝；我娶你，抬的是整座山河。我不是給不起金銀珠玉，是覺得那些配不上你。這江山我一寸一寸打下來，如今我把它折成一紙聘書，遞到你面前——你點個頭，這天下就換一個主母。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配帝王將相、權謀霸總的古裝劇照，或當作「土到極致但很爽」的霸氣告白貼文。
variations: 我要的不是天下第一，是天下第一，只想娶你。
山河是我給你的聘禮，你的一句願意，才是我要的江山。

en.content: Other men marry you with ten miles of red dowry; I marry you by carrying the whole realm to your door. It's not that I can't afford gold and jade — it's that none of it is worthy of you. This empire I took an inch at a time, and now I've folded it into a single betrothal letter and set it before you. One nod from you, and the whole world gets a new mistress of the house.
en.editorNote: For an emperor or scheming-tycoon period still, or as a maximally cheesy-but-satisfying grand confession post.
variations: I don't want to be first under heaven; I want to be the first man under heaven who only wants to marry you.
The realm is my betrothal gift — but your single 'I will' is the empire I actually want.

items.sourceNote: 專情表白「弱水三千只取一瓢」register 參考（亂花叢中獨守一人母題），內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 都說弱水三千，我偏偏只認你這一瓢。不是這世上沒有更好看的、更懂事的，是我這雙眼睛一旦落在你身上，就再也擠不進第二個人。你若問我為什麼，我也答不上來——喜歡一個人哪有什麼道理，有道理的，那叫盤算。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配專情男主、獨寵一人的古裝劇照，或送給那個「見過世面卻只想要你」的人。
variations: 三千弱水我一滴都不貪，就守著你這一瓢，喝一輩子。
不是沒有更好的選擇，是我根本不想選——我的眼裡早就只剩你一個。

en.content: They say there are three thousand waters, but I'll take only this one ladleful — you. It's not that no one prettier or gentler exists; it's that once my eyes land on you, there's no room to squeeze in a second person. If you ask me why, I couldn't tell you — loving someone has no reason. The kind with reasons is called a calculation.
en.editorNote: For a devoted-male-lead or one-person-only period still, or for the one who's seen the world and still wants only you.
variations: Of three thousand waters I won't covet a single drop — I'll keep this one ladleful and drink it for a lifetime.
It's not that there's no better choice; it's that I don't want to choose — my eyes have had room for only you for a long time.

items.sourceNote: 2026 古裝喜劇熱潮（機鋒快問快答、擺爛式生存智慧）register 參考，內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 滿朝文武比的是誰的膝蓋硬，我比的是誰的臉皮厚。他們罵我沒骨氣，我笑著點頭，順便把茶續滿——骨氣這種東西，得先有命，才擺得出來。等哪天我真站直了，你們就會發現：我彎了那麼久，是為了看清楚地上到底掉了些什麼。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配古裝喜劇、腹黑諧星角色的劇照，或當作「在職場先活下來再談原則」的自嘲貼文。
variations: 我不是慫，我是懂得排隊——排在最後面的那個，往往最後才輪到挨刀。
他們比誰站得直，我比誰活得久；到最後站著的那個，才有資格說什麼叫骨氣。

en.content: The whole court competes over whose knees are stiffest; I compete over whose face is thickest. They call me spineless, and I nod along and top up their tea — a spine is something you can only show off after you've stayed alive. The day I finally stand up straight, you'll all realize I spent that long bent over checking what everyone had dropped on the floor.
en.editorNote: For a period-comedy or sly-schemer still, or as a self-deprecating 'survive the office first, have principles second' caption.
variations: I'm not a coward, I just understand queues — the guy at the back is the last one to get stabbed.
They compete over who stands straightest; I compete over who lasts longest. Only the one still standing gets to define backbone.

items.sourceNote: 2026 修仙/武俠劇「書生仗劍」母題 register 參考（文弱書生佩劍出門），內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 他們笑我一個手無縛雞之力的書生，也配在腰上掛劍。我沒爭——這劍我確實揮得慢、拔得笨。可我讀過的那些書告訴我，人這一生總得挑一個地方站著，才不算白走。腰上有沒有劍是其次，心裡那一寸不能空。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配書生型男主、文人拔劍的武俠仙俠劇照，或送給那個「看起來很軟、其實最不肯低頭」的人。
variations: 劍術我學得慢，但我很早就知道，這把劍不能對著誰揮——這已經比很多人快了。
我不是靠這把劍撐著；是這把劍靠著我，才不至於變成一件凶器。

en.content: They laugh that a scholar who can't wring a chicken's neck has no business wearing a sword. I don't argue — I do draw slow and swing clumsy. But everything I've read taught me this: you have to pick a place to stand or the whole walk was for nothing. Whether there's a blade at your hip is secondary; the inch inside your chest can't be empty.
en.editorNote: For a scholar-turned-swordsman still, or for the person who looks soft and is the last one to bow.
variations: I learned swordplay slowly, but I learned early who I must never point it at — which puts me ahead of most people.
I'm not leaning on this sword; the sword leans on me to keep from becoming just another weapon.

items.sourceNote: 2026 神話奇幻古裝劇（神祇視角、香火與願望母題）register 參考，內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 我在這座小廟裡受了三百年香火，聽過的願望比落過的雨還多。有人求金銀，有人求長命，只有你，年年只求我保佑另一個人平安。我這副泥塑的身子，其實什麼也管不了——可你跪下來的那一刻，我第一次很想，真的有靈。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配神話奇幻古裝劇照、廟宇祈願場景，或寫給那個「總是先替別人許願」的人。
variations: 你替全世界求了一輪，最後才輕輕加一句：我沒什麼想要的——那一句，我記了三百年。
神明也有做不到的事；我唯一做到的，是每一年都在這裡，等你來說話。

en.content: Three hundred years of incense in this little shrine, and I've heard more wishes than the roof has caught rain. People ask for gold, for long life. Only you come back every year and ask me to keep someone else safe. This clay body of mine can't actually do anything — but the moment you knelt, I wished, for the first time, that I were real.
en.editorNote: For a mythic-fantasy period still or a temple-prayer scene, or for the person who always spends their wish on somebody else.
variations: You wished for everyone else first, then added quietly, 'There's nothing I want' — I've remembered that line for three hundred years.
Even gods have things they can't do. The one thing I managed was being here every year when you came to talk.

items.sourceNote: 古裝劇「白首偕老」結局 register 參考（晚年回望、粗茶淡飯式深情），內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 年輕的時候我以為情話要說得驚天動地才算數。老了才知道，最狠的一句是——你端來的那碗粥，我喝了四十年，今天嫌它鹹，明天照樣端起來喝完。能一起把頭髮熬白，本來就是這世上最奢侈的事，只是當年沒人告訴我們。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配古裝劇溫馨結局、老夫妻同框畫面，或當作結婚週年、長輩紀念日的貼文文案。
variations: 我這輩子最厲害的成就，不是掙了多少，是把同一個人的脾氣，記熟了四十年。
驚天動地的話我年輕時說完了；剩下的日子，我只想每天問你一句：今天想吃什麼。

en.content: When I was young I thought love talk had to shake heaven and earth to count. Now that I'm old I know the deadliest line is this: I've eaten your congee for forty years, I complained it was salty today, and tomorrow I'll pick up the bowl and finish it again. Going gray beside someone is the most extravagant thing there is — nobody warned us back then.
en.editorNote: For a warm period-drama ending or an old-couple frame, and for anniversary or family-milestone posts.
variations: My greatest achievement isn't what I earned; it's knowing one person's moods by heart for forty years.
I used up all the earth-shaking lines when I was young. All I want now is to ask you daily: what do you feel like eating?

items.sourceNote: 大女主/女將軍題材 register 參考（女子披甲上陣、非為誰而戰母題），內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content: 他們總問我，這一身鎧甲是為誰而穿。為誰？我十六歲第一次上馬的時候，天底下還沒有哪個人值得我為他去死。甲是我自己扛上肩的，仗是我自己要打的。真要說為了誰——就為了讓後頭那些姑娘知道，這身鎧甲，女人也穿得。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配女將軍、巾幗題材的古裝劇照，或當作女性職涯、運動賽事的勵志貼文。
variations: 別替我把功勞算到誰頭上——這條路上的每一道傷，都是我自己換來的。
我不是誰的軍師、誰的紅顏，我是這支隊伍的主帥；名字寫在最前面那個，就是我。

en.content: They keep asking who I wear this armor for. Who? At sixteen, the first time I got on a horse, there wasn't a single person on earth I'd have died for. I hauled this armor onto my own shoulders and picked this fight myself. If it has to be for someone — it's so the girls coming up behind me know that women wear armor too.
en.editorNote: For a woman-general or warrior-heroine still, and for posts about women's careers or sports.
variations: Don't credit my record to anyone else — every scar on this road, I paid for myself.
I'm not someone's strategist or someone's beauty. I command this army; the name at the top of the roster is mine.

items.sourceNote: 2026 古裝陸劇片單（含《唐宮奇案》太史丞一角）激發的史官題材，台詞為原創撰寫，非任何劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 您拿刀逼我改的，不過三個字。可這支筆一旦彎過一次，往後翻到這一頁的人，看見的就是一整個彎掉的年代。命，您取得走；落在紙上那一行，您取不走。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合被要求「數字修一下」「話講漂亮一點」的時候，替自己守住底線；也適合做記錄、報表、報導相關工作的自勉。
variations: 我可以跪，這支筆不能跪。
您燒得掉這一卷，燒不掉我明天再寫一遍的手。

en.content: What you're holding a blade over is three words. But bend a pen once, and everyone who opens this page later inherits a bent century. My life you can take. That line on the paper isn't yours to take.
en.editorNote: For the moment someone asks you to soften the numbers or phrase it more kindly — a spine-stiffener for anyone whose job is keeping the record straight.
variations: I'll kneel. The pen won't.
You can burn the scroll. You can't burn the hand that writes it again tomorrow.

items.sourceNote: 古裝探案／權謀劇常見的獄中場景設定，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 我在這牢裡當了二十年差，一輩子只學會兩件事：上鎖，開鎖。你要我放你走，我做不到。可今夜換我值更，那扇高窗我替你推開半尺——天亮以前，你就當自己還是個能看月亮的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 用在你幫不上大忙、卻還想替人留一點餘地的時候；也適合提醒自己，身在規矩裡的人，依然能選擇多做那半尺。
variations: 規矩我改不了，可我能晚一刻再落鎖。
我這串鑰匙管不了誰的生死，只管得了誰今晚睡不睡得著。

en.content: Twenty years in this jail and I've learned exactly two things: how to lock a door, and how to unlock one. I can't let you walk out. But the night watch is mine, and that high window opens half a foot — until dawn, you get to be a man who can still see the moon.
en.editorNote: For when you can't fix someone's situation but can still leave them a little air; also a reminder that people inside a system still choose how far they'll bend.
variations: I can't rewrite the rules. I can turn the key a minute late.
This ring of keys decides nothing about your life — only whether you sleep tonight.

items.sourceNote: 宮廷劇乳娘／老僕配角視角，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 你三歲那場高熱，是我抱著你在廊下走了一整夜。如今你披上嫁衣進宮，我連喜宴的末席都坐不上——奶娘這兩個字，本來就不算什麼名分。可你要是哪天在裡頭撐不住了，記著：這世上有個老婆子，不圖你的賞、不占你的名，只盼你平安。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫給那些沒有名分卻真的疼過你的人——保母、學姊、老鄰居；也適合你自己默默照顧了誰很久、卻從不出聲的時候。
variations: 我沒有名分，卻替你擋過所有的風。
你長大以後不必記得我，只要記得那一夜，有人抱著你走到了天亮。

en.content: The year you burned with fever at three, I walked you up and down that corridor till morning. Now you're in bridal red on your way into the palace, and I don't even get the last seat at the banquet — 'nurse' was never really a title. But if a day comes when you can't hold up in there, remember: some old woman out here wants nothing from you, claims nothing of you, and only prays you're safe.
en.editorNote: For the people who loved you with no official standing — a nanny, a mentor, an old neighbor; also for when you're the one quietly doing the caring.
variations: No title, no claim — I still stood between you and every cold wind.
You don't have to remember me. Just remember someone carried you through that night.

items.sourceNote: 2026 神話奇幻古裝劇片單激發的月老／姻緣簿母題，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 你們這條線，我繫過三次。第一次遇上戰亂，第二次差了半條街，第三次你們坐同一條船，卻沒抬頭。到了這一世我懶得繫了——結果你們自己在人海裡找到了對方。所以別謝天謝地，該謝的是你們兩個，走得比命還執著。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫給繞了很久才在一起的伴侶，也適合週年、求婚貼文——把「命中注定」的功勞還給願意堅持的兩個人。
variations: 緣分只負責把你們放進同一座城，剩下的那幾步，是你們自己走過來的。
我這本簿子寫得再滿，也抵不過你那句：我再等一年。

en.content: I've tied your thread three times. The first time a war got in the way, the second you missed each other by half a street, the third you rode the same boat and never looked up. This lifetime I didn't bother — and you found each other anyway, in a crowd of thousands. So don't thank fate. Thank the two of you, stubborner than destiny.
en.editorNote: For the couple who took the long way around, and for anniversary or engagement posts — it hands the credit back to the people who kept trying.
variations: Fate only puts you in the same city. Those last few steps you walked yourselves.
Nothing written in my book beats you saying, 'I'll wait one more year.'

items.sourceNote: 古裝甜寵劇常見的醫者／診脈場景設定，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 我行醫十年，天下的脈象沒有一種能瞞得過我。你伸手過來的那一刻，我摸到的不是風寒，是亂——跳得又急又沒章法。我開了三帖藥，一帖都治不好，因為病根是我。這句話我不敢寫進藥方，只好每次都多留一句：明日再來，我替你看看。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合曖昧期的貼文，或用來形容「他一靠近我就心跳失序」；也可以拿來當醫療、照護題材的告白梗。
variations: 脈象我讀得懂，你眼裡的意思我讀不懂——所以我只好一天問你三次，好些了嗎。
我治得好全城的人，唯獨治不好聽見你名字就亂掉的這一顆。

en.content: Ten years of practice and no pulse has ever fooled me. The moment you held out your wrist, what I felt wasn't a chill — it was chaos, fast and out of rhythm. I wrote three prescriptions and not one of them works, because I'm the cause. I can't put that on paper, so I just add the same line every time: come back tomorrow, let me check again.
en.editorNote: For that will-they-won't-they stage, or to describe someone who wrecks your heart rate by walking in; also a soft confession line with a medical twist.
variations: I can read your pulse. I can't read your eyes — so I ask you three times a day whether you're feeling better.
I can cure this whole town. I can't cure the one heart that stumbles at your name.

items.sourceNote: 2026 大女主宮廷／權謀劇 register 參考（卸妝、銅鏡自照母題），台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 他們說我這張臉是進宮最好的本錢。今夜我把珠翠一根一根拔下來，胭脂洗盡，銅鏡裡剩下一個素面的人——她照樣認得帳目、看得懂人心、記得住每個人欠我什麼。所以你們真正忌憚的從來不是這張臉，是拔光了首飾以後，我還在。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合大女主劇照、卸妝素顏照，或寫給那些「總被說靠外表」的人；也能用在職場被低估時替自己撐一句。
variations: 你們喜歡的是我盛裝的樣子，我靠的是我卸妝以後還有的那些。
首飾是借來的，腦子是我自己的——這兩樣，你們搶得走哪一樣？

en.content: They said this face was my best asset for getting into the palace. Tonight I pulled the pins out one by one, washed the rouge off, and the bronze mirror showed a plain-faced woman — who still reads the ledgers, still reads people, still remembers exactly what everyone owes me. So it was never the face you were wary of. It's that with the jewels gone, I'm still here.
en.editorNote: For a leading-lady still or a bare-face photo, and for anyone tired of being credited to their looks; also a spine-stiffener when you're underestimated at work.
variations: You liked me dressed up. I run on what's left when the jewels come off.
The ornaments were borrowed. The mind is mine — which of the two do you think you can take?

items.sourceNote: 宮廷劇底層宮女／浣衣局場景設定，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 前頭殿裡爭的是恩寵，我們在浣衣局爭的是一桶熱水。你那年冬天把手泡爛了，我偷偷把自己那份熱水倒進你的盆裡；你什麼也沒說，只是把懷裡半個冷饅頭掰給了我。這宮裡的情分，貴人們算得清清楚楚，只有我們是用一桶水、半個饅頭記的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫給一起熬過苦日子的同事、室友、同梯；也適合用在「不是誰救了誰，是我們互相撐著」的懷舊貼文。
variations: 我們沒有恩寵可以爭，只有彼此可以護。
那半個冷饅頭，我記到現在——比後來所有人給我的賞賜都暖。

en.content: In the front halls they fight over favor. In the laundry court we fight over a bucket of hot water. The winter your hands split open, I poured my share into your basin; you said nothing, just broke off half a cold bun and handed it over. The great ladies keep careful accounts of who owes whom. We kept ours in buckets of water and halves of bread.
en.editorNote: For the coworkers, roommates, or classmates you got through the lean years with — the kind of bond where nobody rescued anybody, you just held each other up.
variations: We had no favor to compete for — only each other to protect.
I still remember that half a cold bun. It was warmer than every reward I got later.

items.sourceNote: 2026 下半年武俠／修仙古裝劇熱潮激發的師門送別母題（師父視角），台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 招式我教完了，山下的路我不能陪你走。記著——為師這輩子最後悔的，不是輸過幾場，是有一年心軟收了手，害得該護的人沒護住。你可以打不贏，可以認錯，可以回頭；唯獨不能在該站出去的那一刻，替自己找理由。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合送人出社會、送學生畢業、送隊友轉隊的場合；也可以在自己猶豫「要不要出頭」時拿出來看一次。
variations: 我教得了你怎麼贏，教不了你在沒人看見的時候怎麼選。
下了這座山，沒有人再喊你師弟師妹了——從今天起，你自己就是門派。

en.content: I've taught you every form I know; the road down the mountain I can't walk with you. Remember this — my greatest regret isn't the fights I lost. It's the year I hesitated, pulled a strike, and failed to protect someone I should have. You're allowed to lose. You're allowed to be wrong. You're allowed to turn back. What you're not allowed is to talk yourself out of the moment you should step forward.
en.editorNote: For sending someone off — a graduate, a new hire, a teammate moving on; also worth rereading yourself when you're hesitating over whether to speak up.
variations: I can teach you how to win. I can't teach you what you'll choose when nobody's watching.
Once you're off this mountain, nobody calls you junior anymore. From today, you are the school.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年八月檔古裝權謀劇熱潮中常見的暗衛／護衛母題（守在屋梁上的視角），台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 我在你屋梁上待了九年，數得出你每一次翻身、每一場沒睡好的夜。你這輩子大概不會知道我長什麼樣子——這樣最好。要是哪天你抬頭看見了我，那就表示，我已經沒能替你擋住那把刀。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合形容那種默默付出、從不邀功的角色或朋友；也可以配「有些人是在你看不見的地方，替你把事情擋掉了」的貼文。
variations: 我不需要你記得我的名字，只需要你今晚也能睡到天亮。
最好的護衛，是一輩子都沒有機會被你認出來的那一個。

en.content: I've lived in your rafters for nine years. I know every time you turn over in your sleep, every night you don't sleep at all. You'll probably never know my face — and that's how it should be. The day you look up and see me is the day I failed to stop the blade.
en.editorNote: For describing the person who quietly carries things for you and never asks for credit; pairs well with a post about the help you only notice in hindsight.
variations: You don't need to remember my name. You just need to make it to morning.
The best guard is the one you never once had to recognize.

items.sourceNote: 2026 古裝家族劇常見的女兒紅（生女埋酒、出嫁開壇）婚嫁母題，父親視角，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 你出生那年，我在後院埋了一罈酒，說好等你出嫁那天再挖出來。今天挖開了，酒是香的，我卻一口都喝不下——原來這十八年我埋的不是酒，是捨不得。你儘管走，回頭看一眼就好，別走回來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 婚禮致詞、送女兒／好友遠嫁遠行時很好用；也適合寫給任何一個你養大、又必須放手的人。
variations: 這罈酒等了十八年才開，我卻希望它再多埋幾年。
門檻我替你跨低了一點，剩下的路，你要走得比我當年穩。

en.content: The year you were born I buried a jar of wine in the back courtyard, to be dug up on your wedding day. I opened it this morning. The wine is perfect. I can't drink a drop of it — turns out what I buried for eighteen years wasn't wine, it was letting go. Go on. Look back once, then don't come back.
en.editorNote: Made for wedding toasts and send-offs; works for anyone you raised and now have to release.
variations: Eighteen years I waited to open this jar, and now I wish I'd buried it deeper.
I lowered the threshold for you. The rest of the road you walk steadier than I did.

items.sourceNote: 2026 下半年古裝劇常見的渡口／擺渡人離別母題，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 這條河我撐了三十年篙，送過赴考的、逃命的、回家奔喪的，一個都沒落下。他們都以為擺渡的人見多了離別就不痛了——其實我只是學會了一件事：船靠了岸就別再回頭喊，喊了，兩邊都走不動。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合送別、離職、搬家、分手後放下的情境；也可以配「幫別人過河的人，自己站在原地」的心情貼文。
variations: 我送得走所有人，唯獨送不走站在岸上的自己。
上船的時候別問我對岸好不好，我只負責讓你到得了。

en.content: Thirty years I've poled this crossing — students off to their exams, families running from war, sons going home to bury a father. Not one of them missed the boat. People assume a ferryman stops feeling the goodbyes. What I actually learned is simpler: once the boat touches the far bank, don't call out. Call out, and neither side can move.
en.editorNote: For farewells, last days at a job, moving away, or finally closing a chapter; good caption for the feeling of helping everyone else move on.
variations: I can get anyone across. The one I can't ferry off this bank is me.
Don't ask me what the other side is like. My job is only getting you there.

items.sourceNote: 2026 暑期檔七部古裝大劇同期開播引發的追劇日常自嘲，台詞為原創撰寫

zh-tw.content: 我看古裝劇都開兩倍速，權謀跳過、宮鬥跳過、打戲跳過——結果男主角回頭看女主角那三秒，我調回原速看了五遍，還截了圖。所以我不是沒空，我只是把時間，全省下來看那三秒。
zh-tw.editorNote: 追劇族自嘲、暑假檔一次開播好幾部時最有共鳴；配截圖或「我的存圖資料夾」貼文很好用。
variations: 進度條我拉得比誰都快，唯獨那一段，我倒回去看了三次。
別人問我劇情演到哪，我只答得出他們對視了幾次。

en.content: I watch every period drama at double speed — skip the court politics, skip the palace intrigue, skip the fight scenes. Then the lead turns around and looks at her for three seconds and I drop back to normal speed, rewatch it five times, and screenshot it. So it's not that I'm busy. I just save all that time for those three seconds.
en.editorNote: Self-deprecating binge-watcher humor, especially when several costume dramas drop at once; great caption for a screenshot folder post.
variations: Nobody drags the progress bar faster than me — except across that one scene, which I rewound three times.
Ask me what happened in the plot and all I can tell you is how many times they made eye contact.

items.sourceNote: 立秋（2026-08-07）節氣中「秋扇見捐」的古典母題，改寫為宮廷大女主的反轉視角，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 入了秋，我這把扇子就被收進箱底了。宮裡人笑我，說扇子最怕天涼。可我從頭到尾都清楚一件事——不是我不中用了，是這個季節不需要風了。你們把我收起來吧，收得越深越好；等下一個熱天到了，你們自然會記得，是誰替你們搧了整整一個夏天。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合被冷落、被調離、被公司「先放著」的時候發；也適合寫給那個努力被當成理所當然、事後才有人想起的自己。
variations: 我沒有壞掉，我只是被放進了不需要我的季節。
扇子從不解釋自己還能搧風，它只等天再熱起來。

en.content: Autumn came, and my fan went into the bottom of the chest. The court laughs — a fan's worst enemy is cool weather. But I've been clear about one thing all along: it isn't that I stopped working. It's that this season stopped needing wind. Pack me away, then. Pack me deep. When the heat returns, you'll remember on your own who kept you cool all summer.
en.editorNote: For being sidelined, reassigned, or quietly benched at work; also for anyone whose effort was treated as background noise until it was gone.
variations: I'm not broken. I was just put away in a season that had no use for me.
A fan never argues that it still works. It waits for the heat.

items.sourceNote: 立秋「一葉知秋」意象改寫為感情將盡的細微徵兆（宅院／深閨視角），台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 院裡那棵樹落第一片葉子的時候，別人都還在搧扇子，只有我知道秋天到了。就像你昨夜多添了一件外衣、把書信收進了裡層、離開時把門帶得比平常輕——你什麼都沒說，可我全看見了。我不揭穿，只是想把最後這幾天，過得像什麼都沒發生。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫已經察覺對方要走、卻選擇不點破的心情；配落葉、關門、背影類的古裝劇照很有味道。
variations: 你以為藏得很好，其實你已經開始收拾了，只是還沒說出口。
我不是後知後覺，我只是想再多騙自己一個秋天。

en.content: The first leaf fell in the courtyard while everyone else was still fanning themselves. Only I knew autumn had arrived. It's the same as last night — you added a layer, moved your letters to an inner pocket, and closed the door softer than usual on your way out. You said nothing. I saw all of it. I won't call it out. I just want these last few days to feel like nothing is happening.
en.editorNote: For the ache of knowing someone is leaving and choosing not to say so; pairs with falling leaves, a closing door, a figure walking away.
variations: You think you hid it well. You'd already started packing — you just hadn't said it yet.
I wasn't slow to notice. I wanted to fool myself for one more autumn.

items.sourceNote: 農曆七月七「曬書曬衣」古俗（有別於已收錄的穿針乞巧），改寫為書院暗戀母題，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 七月七這天，全院子的人都把書搬出來曬。你那本翻爛的兵書一攤開，掉出一片乾透的葉子——是三年前我夾進去的，你居然一直沒扔。你彎腰撿起來，看了很久，然後夾回原來那一頁。那天我什麼也沒說，只覺得日頭好烈，烈得眼睛有點酸。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合七夕、書單、換季整理的貼文；也適合寫那種「兩個人都知道、卻誰也不先開口」的暗戀。
variations: 書可以曬，心事不能曬——一見光就藏不住了。
你把葉子夾回原處的那一下，比說一百句喜歡還重。

en.content: On the seventh of the seventh month everyone hauls their books out to air in the sun. You opened that battered strategy volume and a dried leaf fell out — the one I slipped in three years ago. You never threw it away. You bent down, picked it up, looked at it for a long moment, and tucked it back on the same page. I didn't say anything. I just noticed the sun was very bright, bright enough to sting my eyes.
en.editorNote: For a Qixi post, a book photo, or a seasonal clear-out; also for the crush where both people know and neither goes first.
variations: You can air out books. You can't air out what you're hiding — one hour of sunlight and it's obvious.
You put the leaf back on the same page. That said more than a hundred confessions.

items.sourceNote: 立秋後「秋老虎」餘熱不退的節氣現象，改寫為古裝商賈／掌櫃的處世清醒語，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 曆書上寫著今日立秋，可你出門看看，日頭照樣曬得人脫層皮。做生意的最不能信的就是這種話——帳面上寫著轉虧為盈，不代表冬天有炭燒；旁人喊你熬過來了，不代表最難的那一段過了。字是給人看的，天氣是給人扛的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫給「別人以為你已經沒事了，其實你還在硬撐」的階段；轉職、創業、還債、病後恢復都很適用。
variations: 立了秋不等於涼了，撐過去不等於好了。
別人替你宣布結束的時候，只有你知道自己還在裡面。

en.content: The almanac says autumn begins today. Step outside and the sun will still take a layer of skin off you. In business you learn not to trust announcements like that — a ledger turning black doesn't mean there's charcoal for winter, and everyone telling you the worst is over doesn't mean it is. Words are written for other people. The weather is something you carry.
en.editorNote: For the stretch where everyone assumes you've recovered and you're still holding on — a new job, a new venture, paying down debt, healing up.
variations: The calendar turning doesn't make it cooler. Surviving it doesn't make it fine.
When other people declare it over, you're the only one who knows you're still inside it.

items.sourceNote: 立秋民俗「貼秋膘」「啃秋」改寫為古裝甜寵土味情話母題，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 娘子，立秋要貼秋膘，這碗肉你吃。什麼？你說怕胖？沒關係，你胖的那幾斤我幫你揹，反正這輩子我扛過刀、扛過債、扛過我娘的嘮叨，多扛你三斤算什麼。冬天要來了，我不求別的，只求你身上有肉、心裡有我。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合立秋、換季、揪人吃飯的貼文；情侶之間互相餵食、互相嫌棄的日常最好用。
variations: 你多吃一口，我冬天就少擔一分心。
秋膘我替你貼，秋天我陪你過，剩下的三個季節也是。

en.content: Eat the meat, love — you're supposed to put on a little weight before autumn. What's that, you're worried about getting fat? Don't be. Whatever pounds you gain, I'll carry. I've carried a blade, I've carried debt, I've carried my mother's opinions. Three extra pounds of you is nothing. Winter's coming. I don't ask for much: some meat on your bones and some room for me in your heart.
en.editorNote: For a seasonal-food post or a dinner invite; perfect for couples who feed each other and complain about it.
variations: Every extra bite you take is one less thing I worry about this winter.
I'll carry the winter weight for you. And the winter. And the other three seasons.

items.sourceNote: 2026 古裝劇流行以傳統行業為背景的家業／匠人劇（如明代徽州墨業題材），此則改寫為燒窯匠人母題，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 這一窯燒了七日七夜，柴是我親手劈的，泥是我親手揉的，火我一刻沒離眼。可窯門一開，是寶還是廢，我說了不算。師父教我的頭一句話就是：十窯九不成。所以我從不在開窯前說大話——盡了力再認命，那叫本事；沒盡力就認命，那叫藉口。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合交件、放榜、面試等結果、開獎前的心情；也適合寫給那種「該做的都做了，剩下的只能交給運氣」的階段。
variations: 能控的我一樣沒少做，不能控的我一句不多說。
不是不怕開窯，是怕自己沒資格失望。

en.content: Seven days and seven nights of fire. I split the wood myself, I kneaded the clay myself, I never let the flame out of my sight. But when the kiln door opens, whether it's treasure or trash is not mine to decide. The first thing my master taught me was this: nine kilns out of ten come out wrong. So I never boast before the door opens. Do everything you can and then accept it — that's skill. Accept it without doing everything — that's an excuse.
en.editorNote: For the wait before a result lands — a submission, an exam board, an interview, a launch. For anyone who has done all they can and has to let the rest go.
variations: I did every part I could control. I say nothing about the part I can't.
It's not the opening I'm afraid of. It's not having earned the right to be disappointed.

items.sourceNote: 2026 高討論度古裝劇多走市井群像路線，此則改寫為當鋪朝奉的處世清醒語，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 在當鋪站櫃三十年，我收過金釵、收過兵符、收過人家壓箱底的嫁衣。每個人把東西推過櫃檯時都說同一句：三個月，我一定回來贖。十個裡頭，回來兩個。所以你別跟我說什麼捨不得——真捨不得的東西，人根本不會拿進這扇門。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫「嘴上說得漂亮、行動說了實話」的人際觀察；分手、被已讀不回、被畫大餅的時候都適用。
variations: 說要回來贖的人很多，真回來的很少。
捨不得是嘴說的，捨得是手做的。

en.content: Thirty years behind the counter of a pawnshop. I've taken in gold hairpins, military seals, wedding robes kept at the bottom of a chest. Everyone slides it across and says the same line: three months, I'll be back for it. Two out of ten come back. So don't tell me how much it means to you. What people truly can't part with never comes through that door.
en.editorNote: For the gap between what people say and what they actually do — a breakup, a friend who went quiet, a promise that keeps getting pushed back.
variations: Plenty of people swear they'll come back for it. Few do.
"I can't bear to lose it" is what the mouth says. The hands already decided.

items.sourceNote: 2026 甜寵古裝劇的職人設定風潮，此則改寫為染坊少東的土味告白，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 我家開染坊的，什麼顏色調不出來？靛青、緋紅、鴉青，下缸三回保證透到底。偏偏遇上你——不用下缸，不用上礬，一眼就染透了，還是那種洗到布都爛了也褪不掉的。師父問我這是哪一味顏料，我說：是命。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合告白、曖昧期、情人節或七夕貼文；配一張染布、漸層色或夕陽照片特別加分。
variations: 別的顏色我調得出來，你這一色我調不出來，只能認。
布染壞了還能漂白，心染上了只能認命。

en.content: My family runs a dye house. Name a color and I can mix it — indigo, crimson, raven blue, three dips and it's through to the fiber. And then there's you. No vat, no mordant, one look and it went all the way through. The kind that stays until the cloth itself falls apart. My master asked what dye that was. I told him: fate.
en.editorNote: For a confession, the almost-dating stage, or a Valentine's post; pairs well with a photo of fabric, a gradient, or a sunset.
variations: Every other color I can mix. Yours I can't. I just live with it.
Ruined cloth can be bleached. A ruined heart just learns to live in the color.

items.sourceNote: 2026 下半年古裝劇多亂世家國題材，此則改寫為城門守吏的離別母題，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 我在這座城門當差十一年，出城的人我一個一個記上，回來的人我一個一個劃掉。冊子上有的名字，劃了；有的名字，我年年翻到那一頁，就繞過去。有人笑我死心眼，可若連守門的都不記得誰還沒回來，這城裡就真的沒人記得了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫離鄉、遠行未歸、戰亂與思念；也適合忌日、紀念日或悼念類的貼文。
variations: 劃掉一個名字很容易，翻過那一頁很難。
我不是在等，我只是不肯當第一個忘記的人。

en.content: Eleven years on this city gate. Every name that goes out, I write down. Every name that comes back, I cross off. Some pages I cross off. Some pages I turn to each year and skip past. People say I'm stubborn about it. But if even the gatekeeper stops counting who hasn't come home, then nobody in this city is counting.
en.editorNote: For posts about leaving home, war, or someone who never came back; works for anniversaries and remembrance.
variations: Crossing out a name is easy. Turning that page is not.
I'm not waiting. I just refuse to be the first one to forget.

items.sourceNote: 2026 下半年武俠大劇《劍來》的「問春風、隨本心」母題，此則重新演繹為師徒對話，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 師父說，遇事拿不定主意，就去山口問那陣風。我問了三年，風一個字也沒回過我。後來才懂——風不答，是因為答案早就壓在我心裡，它只是不肯替我把話說出口。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合猶豫不決、轉職、搬家、分手前後那種「其實早就知道答案」的貼文；配山景或風吹樹梢的照片很搭。
variations: 別人給的答案再漂亮，都不是你走得動的那條路。
問到最後你會發現，你要的從來不是答案，是有人點頭。

en.content: My teacher told me: when you can't decide, go to the mountain pass and ask the wind. I asked for three years. It never gave me a single word. Took me that long to work out why — the wind stays quiet because the answer was already sitting in me. It just wouldn't say it out loud on my behalf.
en.editorNote: For posts about a hard decision, a career change, or a breakup you already knew was coming; pairs well with mountains or wind in the trees.
variations: Someone else's answer can be beautiful and still not be a road your feet can walk.
By the end you realize you never wanted an answer. You wanted someone to nod.

items.sourceNote: 取材自「但願世間人無病，寧可架上藥生塵」的老藥行對聯意象，此則改寫為藥鋪掌櫃獨白，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 這間藥鋪我守了四十年，最盼的是門口冷清。別的行當求生意興隆，我這行不一樣——牆上那幾百格藥材，要是能一格一格生灰、長霉，年年沒人來抓，那才是這條街最好的年成。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合醫護、消防、救難、社工這類「最好用不到我」的職業心情；也適合寫平安、健康的祝福文。
variations: 我這一行做得好不好，不看收了多少銀子，看這條街今年少送了幾個人。
我情願整間鋪子閒到發霉，也不想哪一格見底。

en.content: Forty years behind this apothecary counter, and what I hope for is an empty doorway. Every other trade prays for business. Mine doesn't. Those few hundred drawers on the wall — if they all sat there gathering dust and mold, nobody coming in to fill a prescription, that would be the best year this street ever had.
en.editorNote: For nurses, firefighters, rescue workers, social workers — anyone whose best day is the one where nobody needs them; also works as a wish for someone's health.
variations: You don't measure my trade in silver. You measure it in how many funerals this street didn't have.
I'd rather the whole shop go moldy than see one drawer run empty.

items.sourceNote: 2026 下半年修仙劇《鹹魚飛昇》的躺平修仙設定，此則改寫為同門吐槽的喜劇橋段，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 同門的人搶靈石、搶功法、搶長老名冊上的排名，我什麼都不搶，天天躺在後山曬太陽。他們笑我這輩子沒指望——結果渡劫那天，雷劈了半炷香就自己散了。長老看著天上發愣，說：他身上一絲執念都找不到，這雷要劈什麼？
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合吐槽內卷、加班文化、KPI 競賽；也適合擺爛派用來自我辯護的貼文。
variations: 不是我不上進，是我把上進的力氣，全拿去睡覺了。
贏不了的局，我連上桌都省了——省下來的力氣拿去活久一點。

en.content: Everyone in my sect fought over spirit stones, over techniques, over their rank on the elder's list. I fought over nothing and spent my days napping on the back hill. They said I'd never amount to anything. Then came my tribulation: the lightning crackled for about half an incense stick and just fizzled out. The elder stared at the sky and said, there isn't a single obsession on him. What is it supposed to strike?
en.editorNote: For roasting hustle culture, overtime, or KPI season; also a solid defense of doing the bare minimum.
variations: It's not that I lack ambition. I just spent all of it on sleeping.
If I can't win the game I don't sit down at the table. Saves energy for living longer.

items.sourceNote: 2026 古裝劇市井職人群像風潮，此則改寫為穩婆（接生婆）獨白，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 這城裡大半的人，是我這雙手先接住的。他們長大以後在街上遇見我，多半認不出來——這樣最好。人一輩子只有落地那一聲哭是不用學的，剩下的話都學得太漂亮了。你們記不記得我不打緊，我只求你們，別把那一聲真的，也給弄丟了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合生日、生產、新生兒報喜，也適合寫給長大以後越來越會說場面話的自己。
variations: 你這輩子最誠實的一句話，是在還不會說話的時候喊出來的。
我不指望誰記得我，我只指望你們別忘了自己原本的樣子。

en.content: Most of the people in this city passed through these hands first. They grow up, pass me in the street, and usually don't know who I am — which is how it should be. That first cry is the only sound a person never has to be taught. Everything after that, we learn to say far too well. It doesn't matter whether you remember me. Just don't lose the one honest sound you came in with.
en.editorNote: For birthdays, births, and baby announcements; also for anyone who's noticed how polished and careful their own words have gotten.
variations: The most honest thing you ever said, you said before you could talk.
I don't need you to remember me. I need you to remember what you sounded like.

items.sourceNote: 古裝劇書生暗戀母題，此則改寫為臨帖十年寫他人名字的隱忍告白，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 我臨帖臨了十年，柳體歐體都寫得端正，先生誇我筆下有骨。可我自己清楚，這雙手寫得最順、最不必想的，是兩個從沒出現在任何一本正經字帖上的字——你的名字。寫過幾千遍，一張也沒留，全在洗筆的那盆水裡，化乾淨了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合暗戀、單戀、說不出口的心意；配書法、墨水或舊紙張的照片很有味道。
variations: 別人練字是為了考功名，我練字是為了把兩個字寫得好看一點。
寫得再多也不敢留，留下來就等於承認了。

en.content: Ten years of copying the old masters. My teacher says my brushwork has bone in it. But I know the two characters this hand writes best — the ones it doesn't have to think about — never appeared in any respectable copybook. They're your name. I've written it thousands of times and kept not one sheet. It all dissolved in the basin where I rinse the brush.
en.editorNote: For a crush you've never confessed; pairs beautifully with calligraphy, ink, or old paper.
variations: Other people practice their writing for the exams. I practice so two characters come out beautiful.
I never keep a single sheet. Keeping one would be the same as admitting it.

items.sourceNote: 2026 古裝劇非遺匠人題材風潮（《家業》製墨等），此則改寫為鋦瓷匠獨白，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 你抱這只碗來，說要補得看不出來。看不出來的那叫新碗，不叫補。我這行只做一件事——把裂縫變成一條看得見的線，再拿銅釘一顆一顆咬住它。往後你每回端起它，手都會慢一點、輕一點。你嫌它醜，我倒覺得，一只被人小心捧著的碗，比一只從沒摔過的，多活了好幾十年。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合安慰受過傷的人、聊和好與修復關係；配陶碗、老物件或修補痕跡的照片很有味道。
variations: 補得看不出來的是新的，補得看得出來的才是你的。
裂痕不是拿來藏的，是拿來提醒你，這東西你在乎。

en.content: You brought me this bowl and asked me to make the crack disappear. A bowl with no crack is a new bowl — that isn't mending. My trade does exactly one thing: it turns the break into a line you can see, then bites it shut with copper staples, one at a time. From now on you'll lift it a little slower, hold it a little softer. You call that ugly. I'd say a bowl somebody handles carefully outlives one that never fell, by decades.
en.editorNote: For comforting someone who's been through something, or for a making-up-and-mending-it post; pairs with ceramics, kintsugi, or well-worn objects.
variations: A repair you can't see is just a new thing. A repair you can see is yours.
The crack isn't there to be hidden. It's there to remind you that you care about this.

items.sourceNote: 2026 古裝劇市井職人群像風潮，此則改寫為糖畫師傅獨白，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 我在這條街站了二十年，畫過的龍鳳比城裡任何一座廟都多。有讀書人勸我改行畫紙上的，說糖畫留不住，太可惜。可我這行從頭到尾就沒打算留——小娃兒拿到手，先舉高對著日頭看一眼，再從尾巴開始咬。那一口下去我就知道，這張畫成了。天底下最好的東西本來就不長久，能在化掉以前讓人笑一下，就夠本了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合聊當下、聊短暫的美好，或旅行、演唱會、活動結束的貼文；也適合安慰捨不得散場的人。
variations: 留不住不是可惜，是它本來就該被吃掉。
我畫的不是龍，是那小孩舉高看的那一眼。

en.content: Twenty years on this street. I've painted more dragons and phoenixes than any temple in this city. A scholar once told me to switch to paper — said sugar can't be kept, what a waste. My trade never meant to keep anything. The kid takes it, holds it up to the sun once, then starts biting from the tail. That first bite is how I know the picture worked. The best things were never built to last. If it makes somebody smile before it melts, I've made my money back.
en.editorNote: For posts about impermanence and savoring the moment, or the end of a trip, a show, a season; also for anyone who hates when things wrap up.
variations: It isn't a waste that you can't keep it. It was always meant to be eaten.
I'm not painting a dragon. I'm painting the second a kid holds it up to the light.

items.sourceNote: 古裝劇市井療癒母題，此則改寫為深夜麵攤攤主獨白，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 三更過後，這條街只剩我這一盞燈。來的人我大致認得幾分：剛落了榜的、剛被退了婚的、剛從衙門出來腿還在抖的。他們坐下來只說兩個字——一碗。我也不多問，湯多給一勺就是了。這攤子擺了十七年，我沒勸過誰想開一點——人餓著的時候聽不進道理，吃飽了，多半自己就想通了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合深夜、宵夜、陪伴、療癒主題的貼文；也適合寫給那個從不追問、只默默遞熱食給你的朋友。
variations: 我不勸人，我只多給一勺湯。
人餓著的時候聽不進道理，吃飽了自己就想通了。

en.content: After the third watch, mine is the only lamp left on this street. I can usually guess: failed the exams, got jilted, just walked out of the magistrate's office with their legs still shaking. They sit down and say one word — bowl. I don't ask. I just ladle in a little extra broth. Seventeen years at this stall and I've never once told anybody to cheer up. Nobody can hear good advice on an empty stomach. Fed, most people work it out on their own.
en.editorNote: For late-night, comfort-food, or quiet-support posts; also for the friend who never asks questions and just puts food in front of you.
variations: I don't give advice. I give extra broth.
Nobody can hear good advice on an empty stomach. Fed, they usually figure it out themselves.

items.sourceNote: 古裝劇軍旅／江湖識人母題，此則改寫為老馬夫挑馬獨白，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 將軍們來挑馬，開口問的都是同一件事：這匹能跑多快。我從不答。快馬我養過幾十匹，一半死在半路上。真正的好馬，你得摔過才認得出來——人從背上翻下去，牠不跑，牠站在原地低著頭看你，等你自己爬起來，再讓你上一次。這種馬跑第二快，可陪著人一起活著回家的，向來都是牠。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合聊擇友、擇偶、看人的貼文；也適合寫給那個在你最狼狽的時候，沒有轉身走開的人。
variations: 跑得最快的那匹，多半也是先跑掉的那匹。
你摔下來以後還站在原地等你的，才值得你騎一輩子。

en.content: Generals come to buy a horse and they all open with the same question: how fast. I never answer it. I've raised dozens of fast ones and half of them died on the road. You only learn what a horse is worth by falling off it. The good one doesn't bolt. It stands there, head down, watching you, and waits for you to get up and climb back on. That horse comes in second. It's also the one that gets you home alive.
en.editorNote: For posts about picking friends or partners and reading people; also for the person who didn't walk away when you were at your worst.
variations: The fastest one is usually the first one gone.
The one still standing there after you fall is the one worth riding for life.

items.sourceNote: 台灣七夕「七娘媽生、乞巧」民俗背景（臺灣宗教文化地圖），此則寫成穿越者誤把七夕當情人節的自嘲橋段，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 我剛穿過來那年，掐指算好七夕這天要告白。花買了、詞背了、橋也挑好了，結果整條街連一對牽手的都沒有——姑娘們全在院子裡擺針線、供胭脂，拜的是七娘媽，求的是一雙巧手。我抱著花站到三更，唯一跟我搭話的是隔壁大嬸：這束賣不賣？很多年後我才想通，那一夜也不算白站——從天黑陪我站到天亮、一句都沒笑我的那個人，本來就在旁邊。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合七夕當天發現自己準備過頭、或告白計畫整個落空的時候貼；也適合傳給那個陪你把尷尬計畫走完的人。
variations: 巧我是沒求到，倒是求到一個肯陪我站到天亮的人。
那年我學會一件事：花會謝，肯站在原地陪你的人不會。

en.content: Qixi was my first real mistake in this dynasty. I bought flowers, memorized a speech, picked out the prettiest bridge — and found not one couple on the street. Every courtyard was full of girls laying out needles and thread, praying to the Seven Sisters for clever hands. Nobody was praying for a boyfriend. I stood there holding those flowers until the third watch, and the only person who spoke to me was an auntie asking if they were for sale. Took me years to work out that the night wasn't wasted. The one who stood there with me until sunrise and never once laughed had been right beside me the whole time.
en.editorNote: For the Qixi post where your big plan lands flat; also for the friend who stood in the awkwardness with you and never made it worse.
variations: Didn't get the clever hands. Did get someone who stayed till sunrise.
Flowers wilt. The person who stood there with you doesn't.

items.sourceNote: 2026 古裝劇非遺匠人題材風潮，此則改寫為木匠以榫卯作比的告白，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 我做木工的，這輩子沒在正經活上用過一根釘子。兩塊木頭要接得牢，靠的不是釘，是一邊肯讓出一個凹，一邊肯留出一個凸，合起來連縫都看不見，越搖反而越緊。我這雙手量過上千塊料，從沒失手；偏偏遇上你那天量錯了——不是尺寸不對，是我這才發現，自己天生就缺了一角，缺的那一塊，剛好是你的形狀。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合結婚週年，或那種吵完一架反而更牢的關係；配一張兩個人剛好互補的合照特別好用。
variations: 最牢的接法從來不是釘死，是兩邊都肯讓出一塊。
我缺的那一角，量了三十年才知道是你的形狀。

en.content: Carpentry taught me one thing: I've never used a nail on anything that mattered. Two pieces of wood hold because one side gives up a notch and the other keeps a tongue, the seam disappears, and the harder you shake it the tighter it gets. I've measured a thousand blocks of timber and never cut wrong once — until the day I met you. The measurement was fine. What I found out was that I'd been missing a corner my whole life, and it was shaped exactly like you.
en.editorNote: For anniversary posts and for the relationship that got sturdier after the fight; pairs well with a photo of two people who obviously fit.
variations: The strongest joint isn't nailed shut. Both sides gave something up.
Took me thirty years to measure the corner I was missing. It was you.

items.sourceNote: 古裝武俠劇「一念之差」母題，此則改寫為射手自省的短句語錄，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 箭離弦以前，你有一百種選擇；離弦以後，只剩一種——認。這個道理我是拿半條命換來的，所以這些年我話說得慢、弓拉得慢、應承別人更慢；唯獨認錯這件事，我做得比誰都快。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合你剛把打好的訊息刪掉、慶幸自己沒按下送出的那一刻；配一張很安靜的照片就夠了。
variations: 拉得慢不是怕，是知道鬆手以後就收不回來了。
這輩子我唯一想搶第一的，是認錯。

en.content: Arrows are the whole lesson. Before it leaves the string you have a hundred choices; after, you have exactly one — live with it. I paid for that with half a life, so these days I talk slow, I draw slow, and I promise slower still. The only thing I still do faster than anyone else is admit I was wrong.
en.editorNote: For the moment you deleted the message before sending it; works over anything still and quiet.
variations: Drawing slow isn't fear. It's knowing you can't call it back.
The only race I still try to win is the one to say I was wrong.

items.sourceNote: 古裝劇「掌控與信任」情感母題，此則改寫為放風箏的比喻獨白，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 小時候我以為放風箏是比誰飛得高，後來才知道是比誰的手穩。線太緊會斷，全鬆開就飛走了，收也不是放也不是，全看指頭上肯留的那一寸。這一寸我學了半輩子——前半段我抓得死緊，把兩個人的手都勒出了痕；等我終於肯鬆開一寸，才發現你從頭到尾，根本沒想飛。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫給那個被你管得太緊、卻始終沒走的人；也很適合當和好之後的第一則貼文。
variations: 線是我勒斷的，不是你想跑。
鬆一寸不是不要你，是我終於相信你不會走。

en.content: Kites aren't a contest of height. Took me half a life to learn they're a contest of steady hands. Pull too hard and the line snaps; let go completely and it's gone. Everything happens in the one inch of give you keep between your fingers. For years I held on so tight I left marks on both of us. The day I finally loosened that inch, I found out you were never trying to fly away.
en.editorNote: For the person you held too tightly who stayed anyway; good as the first post after making up.
variations: The line snapped because I pulled, not because you ran.
Loosening my grip wasn't letting go. It was finally believing you'd stay.

items.sourceNote: 2026 農曆七月（8/13 開鬼門）民俗背景與「諸事不宜」禁忌，此則改寫為老媒婆的市井獨白，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 七月一到，滿城的喜事全往後挪，連紅紙都沒人裁了。街坊勸我這個月別出門說親，說怕沖著什麼。我笑笑照走——這條街我走了半輩子，難搞的從來不是那些看不見的，是兩家人坐下來，一個嫌聘禮薄，一個嫌嫁妝輕。你們怕的東西一年只鬧一個月；我怕的東西，天天都在人嘴裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合農曆七月期間發文，也適合任何「人比鬼難搞」的吐槽時刻。
variations: 鬼一年只鬧一個月，人一年鬧滿十二個月。
沖不沖我不敢說，我只知道談不攏的從來不是日子。

en.content: Seventh month rolls in and every wedding in town gets pushed back — nobody's even cutting red paper anymore. The neighbors tell me not to go matchmaking this month. Bad luck, they say. I smile and go anyway. I've worked this street half my life, and the hard part was never the things you can't see. It's two families sitting down, one calling the betrothal gift thin, the other calling the dowry lighter. What you're afraid of acts up one month a year. What I'm afraid of comes out of people's mouths every single day.
en.editorNote: For Ghost Month posts, or any time people turn out scarier than the supernatural.
variations: Ghosts act up one month a year. People keep at it all twelve.
It's never the date that's cursed. It's the terms.

items.sourceNote: 2026 中元普渡（8/27）「普施無主孤魂」民俗核心精神，此則改寫為兒女回憶母親擺桌的溫暖獨白，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 普渡的桌子抬到門口，我娘每年都要多擺一副碗筷。我問是給誰的，她說不知道，就是給那些今晚沒有人喊名字的人。那年收成壞得只剩三塊粗餅，她照樣分成四份。我當時嫌她傻，後來才懂——多出來那一副從來不是擺給誰吃的，是擺給我看的：桌子再小，也得留得下一個沒人記得的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合中元普渡當天分享，也適合寫給那個教會你「多留一份」的長輩。
variations: 多的那一副不是給誰吃的，是給我記著的。
她一輩子沒讀過書，卻把最難的一課教完了：分。

en.content: Every year my mother carried the offering table out to the door and set one extra bowl and pair of chopsticks. I asked who it was for. She said she didn't know — for anyone whose name nobody's calling tonight. The year the harvest failed and we were down to three coarse cakes, she still split them four ways. I thought she was a fool. It took me decades to understand the extra setting was never meant to be eaten from. It was set out for me to see: however small the table, you leave room for someone nobody remembers.
en.editorNote: For Hungry Ghost Festival, or a tribute to whoever taught you to set one more place.
variations: The extra bowl wasn't for them to eat from. It was for me to remember by.
She never learned to read, and still finished teaching me the hardest lesson: share.

items.sourceNote: 古裝劇「師者點醒」母題（科舉、書院設定），此則改寫為私塾先生批文章的對白，呼應八月開學季，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 你問我為什麼把這篇文章判了個丙？字寫得漂亮，典故一個沒錯，起承轉合工整得像拿尺量過。可我從頭讀到尾，讀不出你半分不服氣。這篇你是寫給我看的，寫給考官看的，就是沒寫給你自己看。拿回去重寫。這回不必好看，寫一句你敢認的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合開學、新學期發文，也適合送給那個為了交差而做事的人（包括你自己）。
variations: 工整不算本事，工整還敢說真話才算。
寫得漂亮的人很多，敢認的沒幾個。

en.content: You want to know why I marked this essay down? The calligraphy is lovely. Every allusion checks out. The structure is so tidy it looks measured with a ruler. But I read it start to finish and couldn't find a single line you actually disagreed with. You wrote this for me. You wrote it for the examiners. You never once wrote it for yourself. Take it back and do it again. This time it doesn't have to be pretty — just give me one sentence you'd stand behind.
en.editorNote: For back-to-school season, or for anyone (yourself included) doing work purely to get it turned in.
variations: Tidy isn't the skill. Tidy while telling the truth is.
Plenty of people write it well. Almost nobody signs their name to it.

items.sourceNote: 古裝劇「宿命與自主」母題，此則改寫為街頭相士不敢替自己起卦的告白，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 這條街上的人來找我卜前程、卜姻緣、卜今年宜不宜動土，銅錢一擲，我說得八九不離十。偏偏你走過來那天，我把卦筒抱在懷裡抖了半晌，一支也沒敢倒出來——算出來是好的，我往後就只會坐著等它應驗，不肯自己走過去；算出來是壞的，我這輩子頭一次想試的事，還沒開始就先認了輸。所以這一卦我不起了。今日是不是良辰，我自己說。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合鼓起勇氣告白的那一刻，也適合寫給還在等「時機成熟」的自己。
variations: 這一卦我不起了，日子好不好，我說了算。
算得最準的人，最不敢算的就是自己真正想要的那一件。

en.content: People come to me to read their prospects, their marriages, whether the year favors breaking ground. I toss the coins and I'm right nine times out of ten. Then you walked up, and I stood there holding the stick jar against my chest, shaking it, not letting a single one fall. A good reading and I'd spend the rest of my life sitting around waiting for it to come true instead of walking over to you. A bad one and I'd forfeit the first thing I've ever wanted to try before I'd even started. So I'm not casting this one. Whether today is an auspicious day, I'll decide myself.
en.editorNote: For the moment right before you confess, or for the version of you still waiting on the right time.
variations: I'm not casting this one. I'll say whether today is a good day.
The better you read fortunes, the less you dare read your own.

items.sourceNote: 古裝劇「匠人職人」母題，此則改寫為雕版刻工談失誤與專注，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 這一版我刻了二十天，四百多個字，錯一個，整塊梨木就得推掉重來。學徒常問，能不能把那個字挖掉、另外補一小塊進去？可以啊。可補得再巧，印出來那一格的墨色就是不一樣，懂行的人一眼認得出。所以我這行只分兩種東西：能重刻的，叫錯；不能重刻的，叫債。你們年輕人最怕犯錯，我倒覺得該怕的是另一件——刻的時候心不在這裡，等印出千百張才發現，錯的根本不是那個字。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分享給正在為一個小失誤懊惱的人，也適合貼在自己桌前，提醒「事情做一次就把心放進去」。
variations: 能重刻的叫錯，不能重刻的才叫債。
補得再巧，印出來的墨色還是會說實話：這裡動過手腳。

en.content: This block took me twenty days. Four hundred characters. Get one wrong and the whole slab of pearwood goes back to the pile. My apprentices always ask if we can gouge out the bad character and inlay a fresh piece. Sure we can. But no matter how neat the patch, that one square prints a different shade of black, and anyone who knows the trade sees it instantly. So in my line of work there are only two kinds of things: the ones you can carve again, which we call mistakes, and the ones you can't, which we call debts. You young people are terrified of getting a character wrong. What you should fear is the other thing — carving with your mind somewhere else, and finding out after a thousand impressions that the mistake was never the character.
en.editorNote: For someone beating themselves up over a small slip, or to keep at your own desk as a reminder to be present the first time.
variations: What you can carve again is a mistake. What you can't is a debt.
However neat the patch, the ink tells the truth: something was fixed here.

items.sourceNote: 古裝劇「人間清醒處世」母題，此則改寫為走街磨鏡人談自欺，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 我挑著擔子走街串巷，替人磨銅鏡。磨過的鏡子亮得能數清眉毛，偏偏磨得越亮，回頭找我的人越少。有位夫人磨完只照了一眼，就把鏡子收回箱底，說：從前看不清的時候，還能哄哄自己。這行做久了我就明白——沒人真的怕鏡子，怕的是鏡子從不替你留半分餘地。所以我只管磨鏡，不管磨心。你照或不照，我這攤子照樣擺。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分享給正在逃避某個真相的朋友，也適合寫給那個「決定不再自己騙自己」的時刻。
variations: 沒人真的怕鏡子，怕的是鏡子不肯替你留餘地。
模糊的時候，人還能哄自己一陣子。

en.content: I carry my kit through the lanes, polishing bronze mirrors. When I'm done you can count your own eyelashes in one. And yet the brighter I get them, the fewer people come back. One lady looked into hers exactly once, then packed it away in a chest. She said: when it was blurry, I could still tell myself things. Do this long enough and you learn — nobody is actually afraid of mirrors. They're afraid that a mirror never gives you any room. So I polish the glass and leave the rest alone. Look or don't look; I'll be set up on this corner either way.
en.editorNote: For a friend dodging a truth, or for the moment you decide to stop lying to yourself.
variations: Nobody fears the mirror. They fear that it leaves them no room.
While it was blurry, you could still tell yourself things.

items.sourceNote: 仙俠劇「器物有靈」設定 register 參考，此則改寫為劍中器靈對主人的告白，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 我在這柄劍裡待了八百年，跟過三個人。第一個把我供在架上，逢人就說這是鎮宅的寶；第二個拿我劈開了半座山，說我是把趁手的兵器。只有你，頭一回拔我出鞘的那個晚上，先問了一句：疼不疼。這問題問得毫無道理，一塊鐵哪來的疼。可就是那一問，我八百年來第一次想通——在別人手裡我是「什麼」，在你這裡，我才是「誰」。往後你要斬誰、要護誰，我都跟；哪天你真不用劍了，我去當一根挑水的扁擔，也認。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫給那個「把你當人看，而不是當工具用」的人，也適合形容被真正在乎的瞬間。
variations: 在別人手裡我是「什麼」，在你手裡我才是「誰」。
哪天你不用劍了，我當一根扁擔跟著你也行。

en.content: I've lived inside this sword for eight hundred years and served three owners. The first set me on a stand and told every guest I was the treasure that guarded his house. The second split half a mountain with me and called me a handy weapon. Only you, the first night you drew me, asked something else first: does that hurt. It was a ridiculous question. I'm a piece of iron. But that one question was the first time in eight centuries I understood — in other hands I was a what. In yours I'm a who. Whoever you cut down, whoever you protect, I'm with you. And if you ever put swords away entirely, I'll happily be the pole you carry water with.
en.editorNote: For the person who treats you as someone rather than something, or to describe the moment you first felt genuinely seen.
variations: In other hands I was a what. In yours I'm a who.
If you ever stop carrying a sword, I'll be the pole you carry water with.

items.sourceNote: 宮廷劇「無名者的守護」母題，此則改寫為試菜宮人的獨白，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 每一道菜端上來，都是我先動第一口。銀針驗不出來的東西，得拿人來驗；這宮裡人人都清楚，就是沒人肯說破。旁人替我不值，說我這條命賤得像一道先走一步的影子。我從來沒這樣想過。我先嚐了那一口，你才能安安穩穩把一頓熱飯吃完；我這輩子沒讀過書，講不出什麼大道理，只知道筷子放下的時候，我又替你多換來了一頓飯的工夫。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合形容那些默默替你擋掉麻煩、卻從不邀功的人，也適合寫給家裡最不出聲的那一位。
variations: 這一口我先嚐，換你安穩吃完一頓熱飯。
有些人守著你，是拿自己身上的東西，一點一點換來的。

en.content: Every dish that comes out, I take the first bite. What a silver needle can't detect, a person has to. Everyone in this palace knows it and nobody says it out loud. People tell me it isn't fair, that my life is cheap, that I'm just a shadow sent one step ahead. I've never once seen it that way. I take that bite so you can finish a hot meal without looking up. I never learned to read and I have no grand words for it. I only know that when I set my chopsticks down, I've bought you one more meal's worth of time.
en.editorNote: For the people who quietly absorb trouble on your behalf and never mention it, or for the least vocal person in your family.
variations: I take the first bite so you can finish a hot meal in peace.
Some people protect you by trading away pieces of themselves, one at a time.

items.sourceNote: 古裝市井群像母題，此則改寫為代寫家書的攤販觀察，台詞為原創撰寫，非劇中原句

zh-tw.content: 我在城南擺攤替人寫家書，寫了二十年。來的人多半不識字，一坐下就開始口述：家裡都好、不必掛念、銀子夠用、天冷記得添衣。我一句一句照著寫。寫到最後，十個裡頭有九個會頓一下，聲音壓低半分，說：先生，再加一句——你什麼時候回來。前面那些話，是寫給收信的人聽的；只有最後那一句，是他自己憋了一整年的。所以我這支筆最要緊的本事，從來不是字寫得好看，是等得住那半刻的停頓。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配久未聯絡的家人話題，也適合提醒自己：對方真正想說的，常常在客套話結束以後。
variations: 前面那些「都好」是寫給你聽的，最後那一句才是他真的想說的。
替人寫信這一行，最要緊的本事是等得住那半刻停頓。

en.content: I've run a letter-writing stall on the south side of town for twenty years. Most of my customers can't read. They sit down and start dictating right away: everything's fine here, don't worry about us, the money is enough, put on more layers when it turns cold. I write it all down word for word. And at the end, nine out of ten of them pause. Their voice drops half a step and they say: sir, add one more line — when are you coming home. Everything before that was written for the person receiving it. Only that last line is what they've been holding in all year. So the most important skill in my trade was never good handwriting. It's being able to wait through that half-second pause.
en.editorNote: Good for a message to family you haven't called in a while, and a reminder that what someone really means usually comes after the pleasantries.
variations: All the "we're fine" is for you. The last line is what they actually meant.
In this trade the real skill isn't penmanship. It's waiting through the pause.

items.sourceNote: 古代榜文／告示體例常識背景（官府文告張貼於鬧市要道），此則改採民間告示體撰寫，內容為原創，非劇中台詞

zh-tw.content: 城南牆上這張榜文貼了三年，字淡了就重寫一遍，內容一字沒改過：「尋人。賞銀五十兩。不知姓名，不知籍貫，連長相也記不清楚。只記得那年六月大雨，城外官道塌了半邊，我推的糧車陷在泥裡，過路的人一個接一個繞了開去。有一個人走過去了又回頭，把身上的蓑衣脫下來蓋在米袋上，自己淋著，替我把車推上了坡，撂下一句話就走。三年來上門冒認的有十一個，我一個也沒認錯——那句話，除了他和我，再沒有第三個人聽見。」紙角還添了一行小字：賞銀照舊擺著，你若路過看見了，其實不必來領。我年年重貼這張紙，只是想讓走這條街的人都知道一件事——那天雨下得那麼大，是真的有人回頭了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合用來謝一個當年幫過你、後來卻找不到的人，也適合放在「這世上還是有人會回頭」這類主題的貼文。
variations: 賞銀擺著不是為了找到他，是想讓這條街的人都知道：那天真的有人回頭了。
上門冒認的來過十一個，我一個也沒認錯——那句話，只有他和我聽見。

en.content: Notice on the south wall, posted three years running, rewritten whenever the ink fades, not a word changed. Wanted: one person. Reward, fifty taels. No name, no hometown, no clear memory of the face. Only this: sixth month, heavy rain, half the road outside the city gave way, my grain cart sank in the mud, and one traveler after another walked around it. One man went past, then turned back. He pulled the straw cape off his own shoulders and laid it over the sacks, stood there getting soaked, and helped me push the cart up the slope. He said one sentence and left. Eleven people have come to claim the reward in three years. Not one fooled me, because nobody heard that sentence except him and me. A smaller line runs along the bottom edge: the silver is still set aside, and if you walk past and read this, you do not actually need to come collect it. I repost this paper every year so everyone on this street knows one thing. The rain that day was that heavy, and somebody still turned back.
en.editorNote: For thanking someone who helped you once and vanished, or for a post about proof that people still turn back.
variations: Eleven people came to claim the reward. Not one of them knew the sentence he said.
The silver isn't there to find him. It's there so the street knows somebody turned back.

items.sourceNote: 七夕乞巧穿針與鵲橋民俗背景（《風俗通》使鵲為橋），此則為原創造橋匠人獨白，非劇中台詞

zh-tw.content: 我這輩子修過十七座橋。石頭要挑背陰面出的，樁得打進河床三尺以下，接縫寧可多鑿半個月，也不能省那幾天。橋這種東西成不成，說穿了只看一件事：有沒有人肯在別人趕路的時候，先蹲下去。所以每年到了乞巧這一夜，滿城的姑娘在院子裡穿針求巧，我一個人坐在河邊喝酒。你想想，天上那座最有名的橋，沒用一根木頭、沒鑿一塊石頭，全靠一群鳥肯在那裡站上一夜。我修了一輩子橋，才敢說這句話——橋從來不是材料搭起來的，是有人願意站在那個位置，站到別人走過去為止。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合七夕不想寫情話的時候發，也適合送給那個長期替你撐著、自己卻始終沒走過去的人。
variations: 橋不是材料搭起來的，是有人願意站在那裡，站到別人走過去為止。
天上最有名的那座橋，一根木頭都沒用，靠的是一群肯站一整夜的鳥。

en.content: Seventeen bridges in one lifetime. Quarry the stone from the shaded face, drive the piles three feet into the riverbed, and spend an extra half month on the joints rather than save the days. Whether a bridge holds comes down to one thing: whether somebody will crouch down while everyone else is in a hurry to get across. So on the night of the star festival, while every courtyard in town is threading needles for nimble hands, I sit by the river with a drink. Think about it. The most famous bridge in the sky used no timber and no stone. It held because a flock of birds agreed to stand there all night. A lifetime of building, and this is all I have: a bridge is never made of materials. It is made of someone willing to stay in place until the other person is across.
en.editorNote: Good for a Qixi post when you don't want to write a love line, and for anyone who quietly holds a position so other people can get through.
variations: A bridge is never made of materials. It is made of someone who stays in place.
The most famous bridge in the sky used no timber. Just birds willing to stand all night.

items.sourceNote: 開學季（8/31 開學）情境，古代蒙館開館日與束脩常識背景，此則為原創塾師獨白，非劇中台詞

zh-tw.content: 開館頭一天，爹娘把孩子送進門，束脩擱在案上，說的話都差不多：先生，這孩子交給您了，往後能不能中舉，全看您。我一律點頭收下，回頭翻開兩本冊子。第一本記功名，三十年來我這館裡出過兩個舉人，名字寫在最前頭，紙都黃了。第二本沒給人看過：城東那個算得一手好帳、替全村擋掉一場糊塗官司的，記在第三頁；在市集替鄰里過秤二十年、沒短過人一兩的，記在第九頁；還有一個什麼都沒考上，如今在渡口教小孩認字。我教到這把年紀只認一件事——第一本冊子薄，第二本冊子厚，而一個孩子這輩子過得好不好，多半寫在厚的那一本裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合開學季安撫焦慮的家長與學生，也適合提醒自己：成績單以外的那本冊子，其實厚得多。
variations: 第一本冊子記功名，很薄；第二本記這孩子後來成了什麼樣的人，厚得多。
他們問我這孩子將來能不能中舉，我只答得出他會不會是個站得住的人。

en.content: Opening day. The dried meat goes on my desk and the parents all say the same thing: teacher, he is yours now, whether he passes the exams is on you. I nod and take him in, every time. Then I open two ledgers. The first records honors. Thirty years, two men from this school passed the provincial exam, their names on the front page, the paper gone yellow. Nobody has seen the second ledger. The man on the east side who keeps flawless books and once kept a whole village out of a ruinous lawsuit is on page three. The one who has weighed goods at the market for twenty years and never shorted anybody an ounce is on page nine. There is also a boy who passed nothing at all and now teaches children their characters down at the ferry landing. After all these years I am sure of one thing. The first ledger is thin, the second is thick, and whether a child's life turns out well is usually written in the thick one.
en.editorNote: For the start of the school year, when a student or a parent needs the pressure taken down a notch.
variations: The honors ledger is thin. The one about who the kid became is much thicker.
They ask if he'll pass the exam. All I can tell them is whether he'll stand on his own.

items.sourceNote: 古代以香計時（香篆、百刻香、更香、一炷香的工夫）常識背景，此則為原創製香匠人獨白，非劇中台詞

zh-tw.content: 我做的香不是給神明聞的，是給人算時辰的。香粉要篩到最細，用模子壓成一個回環的篆字，從頭燒到尾剛好一晝夜；上頭刻了一百道刻痕，燒到哪一道，就是什麼時候。打更的靠它，寺裡坐禪的靠它，衙門審案也靠它。做了半輩子，我最有感觸的反而不是準不準，是那句人人隨口都會說的「一炷香的工夫」。聽起來短得不能再短，可我親眼見過：有人在一炷香裡改了主意、退了一門親、把一句拖了十年的話說出口；也有人在同樣一炷香裡什麼都沒做，只是坐著，等它燒完。同一段長度，燒出來的東西天差地遠。所以我從不說自己在賣時間——時間我留不住，我只是替你把它切成看得見的一段，剩下的，你自己填。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合談時間、拖延、或正卡在一個決定上的時候用，也適合配「這段時間你想拿來做什麼」的提問。
variations: 同樣一炷香，有人在裡頭改了一生的主意，有人只是坐著等它燒完。
我不賣時間。我只是替你把它切成看得見的一段，剩下的你自己填。

en.content: One coil of incense, powder sifted fine and pressed into a looping seal script, burns end to end in exactly one full day. A hundred notches cut along it, and wherever the ember sits, that is the hour. The night watch runs on it. The monks in meditation run on it. The magistrate times his hearings by it. Half a lifetime in this trade and what stays with me is not the precision. It is the phrase everybody says without thinking: the time it takes one stick of incense to burn. Sounds like nothing. But I have watched a man change his mind inside that span, call off a marriage, finally say the sentence he had been sitting on for ten years. I have watched another spend the same span doing nothing at all, just waiting for it to go out. Same length, wildly different results. So I never say I sell time. Time I cannot hold. All I do is cut it into a piece you can see. What goes inside it is yours.
en.editorNote: For posts about time, procrastination, or a decision you keep sitting on, and as a prompt: what do you want to put inside this hour?
variations: Same hour of incense. One man changed his life inside it. Another watched it burn out.
I don't sell time. I cut it into a piece you can see. What goes in it is yours.

items.sourceNote: 2026 古裝劇趨勢：女主角轉向女官、女科舉、匠人、將領等專業身分，男主角不再是霸總型帝王。此則為原創對白，非任何劇集台詞。

zh-tw.content:
「臣女不是來謝恩的。」
「哦？那你是來做什麼的？」
「來問陛下一句話。這張榜貼出去，滿城的人只會說陛下開了恩典，破例讓一個女子上榜。可臣女那份卷子，是您親手取的——它到底是不是這一科最好的？」
「……是。」
「那就請陛下把『恩典』兩個字收回去。臣女要的是名次，不是賞。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合被說「你有今天是人家給你機會」的時候使用，也適合女性職涯、升遷、爭取署名權的貼文。
variations: 請陛下把「恩典」兩個字收回去。臣女要的是名次，不是賞。
破例不算數。要嘛我這份卷子是最好的，要嘛您就別貼這張榜。

en.content:
"I did not come to thank you, Your Majesty."
"No? Then what did you come for?"
"To ask you one question. Once that list goes up, the whole capital will say you granted an exception and let a woman onto it. But you read my paper yourself. Was it the best paper of this examination or was it not?"
"...It was."
"Then take the word 'exception' back. I came for a rank, not a favor."
en.editorNote: For when someone says you only got here because you were given a chance. Works for posts about women at work, promotions, or fighting for credit.
variations: Take the word 'exception' back. I came for a rank, not a favor.
Either my paper was the best one, or don't post the list at all.

items.sourceNote: 陸劇權謀線經典命題「熟人背刺」的原創改寫，未引用任何既有台詞。

zh-tw.content: 最難防的從來不是背後那一刀。是遞刀的人，先喊了你一聲「自己人」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合被熟人擺一道之後發，或用在聊職場信任、合夥翻臉的貼文。
variations: 刀不可怕。可怕的是那把刀，是我親手交出去的。
背叛從來不從敵人那邊來，敵人根本靠不了那麼近。

en.content: The knife in your back was never the hard part. The hard part is that whoever handed it over called you family first.
en.editorNote: For the aftermath of being burned by someone close. Works for posts about trust at work or a partnership going bad.
variations: The knife isn't the problem. I'm the one who handed it to them.
Betrayal never comes from your enemies. They can't get close enough.

items.sourceNote: 武俠劇常見的江湖客棧場景設定（老闆娘、寄刀、房錢先付）之原創發揮，非任何劇集台詞。

zh-tw.content:
本店三條規矩，寫在門板上，識字的自己看，不識字的我念一遍。
一、刀劍寄放櫃檯。砍壞的桌椅照價賠，我不管你是哪家的少俠、師承何人。
二、恩怨出門左轉。隔壁那條巷子夠寬，打完記得回來吃飯，湯我替你溫著。
三、房錢先付。你們江湖人最愛說「後會有期」——這四個字在我這裡，不能換成銀子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合開店、接案報價、先小人後君子的貼文，也適合聊人際界線怎麼講清楚。
variations: 恩怨出門左轉，打完記得回來吃飯，湯我替你溫著。
你們最愛說「後會有期」——這四個字在我這裡不能換成銀子。

en.content:
Three house rules, painted on the door. If you can read, read them. If you can't, I'll say them once.
One. Blades stay at the counter. You break a table, you pay for the table. I don't care whose disciple you are.
Two. Take your grudges out the door and turn left. The alley is wide enough. Come back for dinner after. I'll keep your soup warm.
Three. Room's paid up front. You wandering types love saying "until we meet again." That line doesn't spend here.
en.editorNote: For posts about opening a shop, quoting a price, or setting terms before the work starts. Also good for talking about boundaries.
variations: Take your grudges out the door and turn left. Come back for dinner. I'll keep the soup warm.
You people love saying "until we meet again." That line doesn't spend here.

items.sourceNote: 當代追劇日常的原創觀察，呼應復仇題材古裝劇的收尾邏輯，非引用內容。

zh-tw.content:
我媽陪我追古裝劇，權謀她不看，打戲她嫌吵，整齣戲她只問三句：這孩子今天吃飯沒？他娘知不知道他在外頭這樣拚？那個壞人有沒有報應？
昨晚男主角終於報了大仇，我在旁邊哭得亂七八糟，她只說了一句：「很好，那他現在可以去睡覺了。」
我本來想笑她看不懂，後來想想——這齣戲鋪了四十集的血海深仇，最後想給那個人的，好像也就是這個。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合追劇心得文，或聊爸媽看戲的角度、聊「拚完之後總得有人叫你去休息」。
variations: 我媽看古裝劇只關心三件事：吃飯沒、他娘知不知道、壞人有沒有報應。
「很好，那他現在可以去睡覺了。」四十集的仇，我媽一句就結案了。

en.content:
My mom watches period dramas with me. She skips the court intrigue, complains the fight scenes are loud, and asks the same three questions all season: has that boy eaten today? does his mother know he's out there working himself to death? and does the villain get what's coming to him?
Last night the hero finally got his revenge. I was a mess. She said, "Good. Now he can go to bed."
I almost laughed at her for missing the point. Then I thought about it. Forty episodes of blood debt, and what the story wanted for him at the end was pretty much exactly that.
en.editorNote: For posts about what you're watching, or about how your parents watch things, or about needing someone to tell you the fight is over and you can rest.
variations: My mom's only three questions about any period drama: has he eaten, does his mother know, and does the villain pay.
"Good. Now he can go to bed." Forty episodes of revenge, closed in one line.

items.sourceNote: 2026 古偶劇「雙強／反差配對」趨勢（女將領配文弱書生）的原創情境改寫，非任何劇集台詞。

zh-tw.content:
滿城都說我這門親事虧了：一個提刀上馬的人，偏偏嫁了個連弓都拉不開的書生。
他們沒見過我卸甲的樣子。甲一脫，肩上那兩道勒痕紅得嚇人，我自己伸手還摸不到。他不會武，可他記得藥膏收在哪一格抽屜、記得力道要多輕、記得我怕痛卻死不肯喊。
這樁婚事划不划算，全城的人都替我算過。只有他從來沒算——他只是每次都先把藥膏在手心裡焐熱了，才敢往我背上抹。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合婚戀、伴侶日常的貼文，也適合聊「外人只看得見條件，過日子的人看得見傷口」。
variations: 他們算的是這門親事划不划算；他算的是藥膏夠不夠溫。
我扛得動甲，扛不動自己背上那兩道痕——那是他的事。

en.content:
The whole city says I married down. A woman who rides into battle, wed to a scholar who can't draw a bow.
They've never seen me take the armor off. Two raw stripes across the shoulders, red enough to scare you, and I can't reach them myself. He can't fight. But he knows which drawer the salve is in, how light the pressure has to be, and that I hate pain and will never once say so.
Everyone in town has done the math on whether this match was worth it. He's the only one who never has. He just warms the salve in his palms first, every time, before he touches my back.
en.editorNote: For posts about marriage and the small daily parts of a relationship, or about how outsiders see the résumé and only one person sees the bruises.
variations: They're calculating whether the match was worth it. He's calculating whether the salve is warm enough.
I can carry the armor. It's the marks it leaves that I need him for.

items.sourceNote: 2026 暑期古裝劇熱門設定「同門同窗走向宿敵對立」之原創對白發揮，非任何劇集台詞。

zh-tw.content:
「你我出自同一個師門，同一本劍譜抄過三遍，連握劍的手勢都一模一樣。」
「所以呢？」
「所以我到今天還想不通，你是從哪一步開始，把當年抄的那些字反著用。」
「不是哪一步。是你每次都替我把師父的板子接下來的那些回。你肯擋在前頭的時候，我學會的其實是——只要有人肯擋，做什麼都行。」
「那你今日站在這裡，是要我再擋一次？」
「不是。我今日站在這裡，只想看看你還肯不肯。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合聊「曾經最靠近的人站到了對面」的貼文，也適合追劇心得談宿敵 CP、師門情誼變質、雙男主／雙女主對立線。
variations: 同一本劍譜抄過三遍，最後拿它來對付彼此的，也只有我們兩個。
我不是恨你變了，我是恨你變的那一步，是我親手扶著你走的。

en.content:
"We came out of the same school. Copied the same sword manual three times over. Even our grip is identical."
"And?"
"And I still can't work out which step you took that made you start reading all of it backwards."
"There wasn't a step. There were all the times you took the master's cane for me. Every time you stood in front, what I actually learned was this: if someone's willing to take the hit, you can do anything you want."
"So you're standing here today to make me take it one more time?"
"No. I'm standing here to find out whether you still would."
en.editorNote: For posts about someone who was once closest to you ending up on the other side, or for drama commentary on rival pairings and mentorships that curdle.
variations: We copied the same manual three times. We're also the only two people who ever used it on each other.
I don't hate that you changed. I hate that I was the one holding you steady while you did.

items.sourceNote: 古裝劇大女主線常見的「和離／自立」命題，以條列式和離書形式原創改寫，非任何劇集台詞。

zh-tw.content:
和離書我自己寫，你看清楚：
一、這門親事是兩家談成的，不是我求來的；今日散了，也不是我求走的。
二、鋪子裡的帳我理了六年，哪一筆是我娘家的本、哪一筆是你添的，冊子攤在桌上，你慢慢對。
三、外頭要怎麼傳，隨他們。說我善妒也好、無出也好，這幾年我沒虧待過這府裡任何一個人，這句話我敢站到祠堂前說。
四、你日後若過得不好，別回頭找我。我不是誰的退路，我是這座宅子裡唯一一個，自己走出去的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合聊離開一段關係、離職、退出某個圈子的貼文，也適合大女主劇單、獨立宣言型文案。
variations: 說我什麼都行，但這幾年的帳，一筆一筆都對得起。
我不是誰的退路。退路是留給還想回頭的人的。

en.content:
I wrote this letter of separation myself. Read it carefully.
One. This match was arranged between two families. I never asked for it, and I am not asking for it to end either.
Two. I have kept the shop's books for six years. Which sums came from my family and which you put in — the ledgers are open on the table. Take your time.
Three. Let people outside say what they like. Call me jealous, call me barren. I have not wronged a single person in this house, and I would say so standing in front of the ancestral hall.
Four. If things go badly for you later, do not come looking for me. I am nobody's fallback. I am the one person in this household who walked out on her own feet.
en.editorNote: For posts about leaving a relationship, quitting a job, or walking away from a circle, and for independence-themed captions.
variations: Say what you want about me. Every line in those books balances.
I'm nobody's fallback. Fallbacks are for people who still plan to turn around.

items.sourceNote: 陸劇朝堂權謀線「賞賜即束縛」命題的原創短句改寫，未引用任何既有台詞。

zh-tw.content: 滿朝都羨慕我這身官服繡得體面，沒人留意另一件事——這衣裳越合身，越說明早就有人把我從頭到腳量過一遍了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合聊職場升遷、被重用其實是被綁住的貼文，也適合權謀劇的清醒系金句配圖。
variations: 賞賜看著是恩典，其實是尺；每量你一次，就把你往裡收一寸。
衣裳合身到這個地步，就不是賞了，是量身做的籠子。

en.content: The whole court envies how well these robes are embroidered on me. Nobody notices the other part: the better they fit, the more certain it is that someone measured me from head to foot a long time ago.
en.editorNote: For posts about promotions and being 'valued' at work when it really means being tied down, or as a clear-eyed caption for political-drama posts.
variations: A reward looks like a favor. It's a ruler. Every measurement pulls you an inch further in.
Robes that fit this well aren't a gift. They're a cage cut to size.

items.sourceNote: 2026 古偶劇熱門「契約婚姻／先婚後愛」設定（世家子與擅理帳的女主）之原創情境改寫，非任何劇集台詞。

zh-tw.content:
成親之前我們簽了三年的契：他要一個能替他理帳的人，我要一間不必看誰臉色的屋子。銀貨兩訖，誰也不欠誰。
頭一年我把他家的爛帳翻了個底朝天，替他省下的銀子，比我娘家攢了一輩子的還多。他從沒誇過我一句，只是每回我熬著對帳，桌角就會多出一碟溫著的點心。
三年期滿那晚，我把契書推過去：算清楚了，一分不差。
他看也沒看，把紙折了兩折收進袖裡，說：「夫人哪裡都算得精，就這一筆算錯了——我當初要的不是理帳的人。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合聊契約式關係、先婚後愛、日久生情的貼文，也適合放在情人節、結婚週年或古偶劇單推薦文。
variations: 他從沒誇過我一句，只是我熬夜那幾晚，桌角的點心一直是溫的。
「夫人哪裡都算得精，就這一筆算錯了。」

en.content:
Before the wedding we signed a three-year contract. He needed someone to straighten out his family's accounts; I needed a room where I didn't have to read anyone's face. Paid in full, nothing owed either way.
In the first year I tore through their books and found more silver than my own family had saved in a lifetime. He never praised me once. He just left a small warm plate at the corner of the desk on every night I sat up with the ledgers.
The night the third year ended, I pushed the contract across to him. Settled, I said. Down to the last coin.
He didn't even look at it. He folded the paper twice, tucked it into his sleeve, and said, "You count everything correctly, madam. This one entry you got wrong. What I needed was never a bookkeeper."
en.editorNote: For posts about arrangements that turn into something real, slow-burn love, or anniversaries — and for period-drama recommendation threads.
variations: He never praised me once. The plate at the corner of my desk was just always still warm.
"You count everything correctly, madam. This one entry you got wrong."

items.sourceNote: 武俠／修行題材常見的「登山問道」場景之原創改寫，非任何劇集台詞。

zh-tw.content:
山下的人問我：爬了這麼多年還沒到頂，累不累？我說累。
他又問：那怎麼不下來？
我指了指身後。這條路本來沒有，是我一步一步踩出來的——我要是不往上走了，後頭的人就沒路可走。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合勵志、堅持、開創型的貼文，也適合送給正在做沒人做過的事、或帶著新人往前的人。
variations: 這條路本來沒有，是踩出來的。停下來，它就長回去了。
我不是為了到頂才走，是因為後頭還有人要走。

en.content:
Someone at the foot of the mountain asked me: all these years climbing and still not at the top — doesn't it wear you out? I said yes.
Then he asked why I don't come back down.
I pointed behind me. There was no path here. I've been stepping it into the rock. If I stop climbing, the people behind me have nowhere to walk.
en.editorNote: For posts about persistence, building something from nothing, or mentoring the people coming up behind you.
variations: There was no path here. It exists because someone kept walking. Stop, and it grows back over.
I'm not climbing to reach the top. I'm climbing because someone is behind me.

items.sourceNote: 七夕／七娘媽為兒童守護神、滿十六歲答謝的民俗背景之原創改寫，非任何劇集台詞。

zh-tw.content: 娘替我拜了十六年七娘媽，昨夜最後一次。她說：不是不求了，是你該自己走了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合七夕、孩子成年或離家獨立的貼文，也適合寫給正在放手的父母。
variations: 她不是不再擔心，只是把香收起來，讓我自己走。
拜了十六年的那雙手，昨夜收了香。

en.content: Mom prayed to the children's goddess for sixteen years. Last night was the last. She said: not that I stopped — you walk it yourself now.
